title: Suspected alcohol poisoning
summary: A person who has drunk too much alcohol can stop breathing, choke on vomit, or become dangerously cold. They need watching closely, not 'sleeping it off' alone.
steps: Stay with the person. Do not leave them alone.
Check whether they respond. If they are unresponsive, breathing badly, or breathing very slowly, call for emergency help immediately.
Place them on their side in the recovery position so vomit does not block the airway.
Keep them warm with a blanket or jacket — alcohol drops body temperature.
Loosen tight clothing around the neck and chest.
Check breathing every few minutes. Be ready to wipe vomit from the mouth.
Note how much they drank and any other substances — give this information to medics.
avoid: Do not leave them lying on their back — they may choke if they vomit.
Do not give them coffee, food, or more water to 'sober them up' — this does not work and can cause choking.
Do not put them in a cold shower or rub them with snow.
Do not assume sleep is safe — heavy drinkers can stop breathing in their sleep.
whenToEscalate: Emergency immediately if: they are unresponsive or cannot be roused, breathing is slow or irregular, lips or fingers look blue or pale, they are vomiting while unresponsive, they have had a seizure, or their skin is cold and clammy.
Any combination of alcohol with other drugs or medicines — emergency.
Young people, small adults, and anyone unfamiliar with alcohol — go to medical care earlier.
